definition: A synthetic option replicates the payoff of an option using a combination of other options and forwards; a straddle is one specific type of synthetic option, formed by buying a put and a call with the same underlying, strike price, and expiration date.
core_idea: Traders can recreate an option-like payoff profile by combining other options and forwards (a synthetic option), and a straddle is a named example of this built from a matching put and call.
key_points: Synthetic option: duplicating the payoff of an option using a combination of other options and forwards.
Straddle: a synthetic option created by buying a put and a call option sharing the same underlying, strike price, and expiration date.
relationships: Straddle is a specific instance of a synthetic option
